newsitem.title: JAPAN: China seen as growth market for platinum jewellery.
newsitem.headline: China seen as growth market for platinum jewellery.

text.p: China is emerging as a strong, although still small, market for platinum jewellery, an official from leading platinum group metals refiner Johnson Matthey plc, said on Tuesday.

Johnson Matthey's interim 1996 platinum review estimated Western platinum sales to China for calendar 1996 at 180,000 ounces, up from 130,000 ounces last year, said Alison Cowley, an executive of the company's precious metals marketing division.
Western platinum sales to China in 1994 were 50,000 ounces and sales in 1993 were 20,000 ounces, the report said.

The jump in imports in 1995 and 1996 was also partly due to a general upgrading in industrial production capacity and an increase in demand from the chemical industry, for use in artificial fibres and petrochemicals.
Platinum use in jewellery will total 100,000 ounces in 1996, surpassing platinum for jewellery use in the United States, the report said.
"China has a large growth potential, especially for the platinum jewellery sector. Chinese demand from the jewellery sector could more than double by the end of this century," Cowley said.
Urban buyers in China were beginning to look at white metal jewellery such as platinum, Johnson Matthey said.
